Job Description

TL;DR

The next wave of stablecoin adoption is payments. We are building a stablecoin clearinghouse to make stablecoins move like money, not a trading asset. We need a backend engineer who can own the systems that move real value: mint and burn flows, reserve accounting, reconciliation, settlement, integrations, and the APIs built on top of all of it.

About Us

We believe stablecoins are better money and will be the backbone of better payments. We see key structural problems hindering stablecoin adoption, and we're going to fix them, starting with building a clearinghouse. We're a small, scrappy team (~10 people) based in NYC, we've raised $10M from a16z crypto and other excellent partners, and we're going to bring better money to the world.

What You’ll Do

Design, build, and operate core backend services behind mint/burn flows, reserve accounting, reconciliation, and settlement pipelines.
Integrate with banks, custody providers, stablecoin issuers, blockchains, and partner APIs, and make those dependencies safe enough for money movement.
Build durable reconciliation and audit trails so the team always knows where money is, what happened, and whether state matches reality.
Design secure API surfaces and own monitoring, alerting, runbooks, and incident response for services that move real value.
Contribute to the payments API and internal/admin surfaces where backend ownership meets customer or operations workflows.
Identify and pursue improvements that make the core product more robust, without waiting for a fully specified ticket.

What We’re Looking For

5-12 years of production backend engineering experience, with services you have designed, shipped, and operated in production. Our stack is TypeScript on Node.js, PostgreSQL, and GCP.
Experience with high-value transactional systems: payments, banking integrations, fintech infrastructure, trading or exchange infrastructure, ledgering, or stablecoin/crypto infrastructure.
A working command of distributed systems fundamentals: consistency, eventing, idempotency, retries, durable reconciliation, ordering, partial failure, and observability.
Judgment for integrating with unreliable external systems: banks, payment rails, custody providers, issuers, or similar partner APIs.
Experience designing secure APIs, handling secrets and access control, instrumenting services, and writing runbooks for infrastructure that moves real value.
Comfort translating ambiguous business and compliance requirements into technical systems, and explaining the tradeoffs to stakeholders across the company.
Willingness and ability to work in person in New York City five days a week. Relocation support is available.

Nice To Have

Direct stablecoin or crypto infrastructure experience: on-chain/off-chain reconciliation, wallet or custody flows, mint/burn, chain finality, or reserve flows.
Background at a payments or fintech company such as Stripe, Plaid, Circle, Paxos, Coinbase, Modern Treasury, or Bridge.
Compliance-adjacent engineering experience: KYC/KYB, AML, sanctions, audit evidence, or reserve attestations.
Ability to build or contribute to admin dashboards, API docs, or partner-facing workflows when needed.
Experience with Temporal or TigerBeetle.
Experience with Rust or Python.
Enthusiasm for building and running core infrastructure with AI coding agents, and helping shape our AI-first engineering culture.

Our Values

Be offended by the status quo. A payment taking 3 days and costing 3% is offensive. Every day that people interact with legacy financial infrastructure costs humanity time and money. Bring the future forward with righteous indignation.
Be all over it. Operate with extreme urgency and accountability. Know the numbers, meet the right people, answer every email, go the extra mile. Ask yourself: can it be done today?
We sell trust. Trust is easy to lose. Security and integrity are our foundation. Use every interaction and every product as an opportunity to build trust. This is non-negotiable.
Do the dishes. We are all owners. Put ego aside and get things done.
Be the glue. Pick each other up and make each other better. Be direct, be helpful, and assume positive intent. Win as a team.
We enjoy the crucible. We are on a mission to change money. It takes a lot of optimism to attack such an ambitious goal. Our opportunity is a privilege and we don't forget that, especially when the journey is hard.

If these values speak to you, come talk to us!

Competitive salary and equity
Comprehensive insurance (medical, dental, vision)

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer to own the accounts and ledgering spine of our RCM platform. This is the path from "insurance paid us" to "the books balance, the patient knows what they owe, and leadership can trust the numbers."

The team is designing and building the next generation of our account and ledgering system. We're moving toward an event-oriented financial model where every charge, payment, adjustment, and refund is immutable. Balances get derived from history rather than maintained by hand. Reporting should fall out of the design, not be stitched together afterward.

Your Team Owns The Full Money Path

The insurance ledger append-only entries recording payer payments, contractual adjustments, denials, and patient responsibility buckets per procedure, with reversal/refund chains for corrections
Posting and adjustment engines that turn remittances into ledger entries and automatically write off, rebucket, or transfer amounts to patient responsibility based on customer rules
Patient account ledgers tracking balance, payments, credits, and refunds that drive statements, the patient portal, and collections
Bank reconciliation — matching insurer checks to actual bank deposits (via bank APIs, BAI2 files, OCR'd deposit slips) so we only post against verified dollars
Reporting ledger and AR — procedure-level rollups, point-in-time views, AR aging, collections reports, plus drift detection when operational balances disagree with reports
An emerging unified event stream that will become the backbone of a cleaner, replayable ledger architecture

What You’ll Do

Design the next-generation account and ledger model, immutable events, derived balances, clear semantics around payer balance vs. patient balance vs. adjustments vs. cash, with invariants that make it structurally impossible to "print money"
Keep operational balances and financial reports in lockstep. Posting, adjustments, patient balances, rollups, and balance reports need to agree. When they don't, we need drift detection and self-healing
Reconcile three (or four) sources of truth: billed charges, payer remittances, bank deposits, and financial reports. Surface discrepancies before customers do
Scale idempotent, explainable posting and adjustment pipelines across high transaction volumes using negation/reversal semantics instead of mutable edits
Operate money-critical systems on very large Postgres tables, safe migrations, trigger-driven projections, backfills, observability, and incident response where "eventually consistent" isn't acceptable

8+ years building software, with a track record of Staff-level work, architecture ownership, mentoring, cross-team influence

The team is designing and building the next generation of our account and ledgering system. We're moving toward an event-oriented financial model where every charge, payment, adjustment, and refund is immutable. Balances get derived from history rather than maintained by hand. Reporting should fall out of the design, not be stitched together afterward.

Your Team Owns The Full Money Path

The insurance ledger append-only entries recording payer payments, contractual adjustments, denials, and patient responsibility buckets per procedure, with reversal/refund chains for corrections
Posting and adjustment engines that turn remittances into ledger entries and automatically write off, rebucket, or transfer amounts to patient responsibility based on customer rules

Bank reconciliation — matching insurer checks to actual bank deposits (via bank APIs, BAI2 files, OCR'd deposit slips) so we only post against verified dollars

An emerging unified event stream that will become the backbone of a cleaner, replayable ledger architecture

Design the next-generation account and ledger model, immutable events, derived balances, clear semantics around payer balance vs. patient balance vs. adjustments vs. cash, with invariants that make it structurally impossible to "print money"

Scale idempotent, explainable posting and adjustment pipelines across high transaction volumes using negation/reversal semantics instead of mutable edits

Make pragmatic calls that weigh security, correctness, reliability, performance, and simplicity against how fast we need to ship.
Mentor Senior and Staff engineers, run architecture and design reviews, and push the technical bar higher through clear direction, strong engineering habits, and honest feedback.
Take real ownership in a fast-moving environment. Spot systemic risks early and fix the root cause instead of patching around it.

Strong backend engineering (Python preferred) and deep experience with relational databases at scale: query performance, ACID transactions, safe migrations, data integrity
Real experience designing or operating financial systems, payments, billing, reconciliation, accounting, or ledgers. You get double-entry accounting, append-only ledgers, idempotency, reversals, and why balances need to be derived from immutable history

We are seeking an experienced Senior Software Engineer
to design, build, deploy, and support enterprise applications across the Salesforce and AWS ecosystems. This role requires strong Salesforce development expertise, including Apex, Aura Components, and Lightning Web Components (LWC), along with hands-on experience developing Java applications and deploying and managing them in AWS.
The ideal candidate combines strong software engineering fundamentals with practical cloud operations experience. They will work closely with product owners, architects, administrators, and engineering teams to deliver secure, scalable, maintainable solutions and reliable integrations between Salesforce, Java services, AWS, and other enterprise systems.

How You'll Shine:

Design, develop, test, and maintain Salesforce applications using Apex, Aura Components, Lightning Web Components, SOQL, SOSL, and Salesforce APIs. Build scalable, reusable Salesforce solutions that follow platform limits, security requirements, and development best practices.
Develop and maintain enterprise Java applications, APIs, microservices, batch processes, and system integrations. Design secure integrations using REST, SOAP, event-driven, and asynchronous patterns.
Deploy, configure, monitor, and support Java applications running in AWS. Work with AWS services such as EC2, ECS, EKS, Lambda, API Gateway, RDS, S3, CloudWatch, IAM, and related networking services, as appropriate. Monitor application health, performance, availability, security, and cost; troubleshoot production issues and implement lasting corrective actions.
Build and maintain automated CI/CD pipelines for Salesforce and Java/AWS applications. Conduct code reviews and establish standards for testing, source control, documentation, observability, and deployment. Participate in release planning, production support, incident response, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Collaborate with technical and business stakeholders to translate requirements into effective technical solutions. Mentor engineers and provide technical leadership throughout the software development lifecycle.

Travel Requirements:

Less than 10%. Travel to different business units or sites may be necessary.

What You'll Bring:

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology/Computer Science or related field.
Master’s degree is a plus.
Preferred: Salesforce certifications such as Platform Developer I, Platform Developer II, or Application Architect.
Preferred: AWS certifications such as AWS Certified Developer, Solutions Architect, or DevOps Engineer.
Strong troubleshooting, communication, and technical decision-making skills.
Preferred: Experience working in Agile product development environments.
Experience with Git, automated testing, code review, and CI/CD practices.
Preferred: Familiarity with observability platforms, application performance monitoring, and production incident management.
Strong hands-on Salesforce development experience with Apex, Aura, and LWC.
Proficiency with Salesforce data modeling, SOQL, platform security, governor limits, asynchronous processing, and integration patterns.
Strong Java development skills, including experience with frameworks such as Spring or Spring Boot.
Experience deploying and operating Java applications in AWS production environments.
Working knowledge of AWS infrastructure, IAM, networking, logging, monitoring, scalability, availability, and cost management.
Experience with RESTful APIs, distributed systems, relational databases, and asynchronous messaging.
Preferred: Experience with Copado and automated Salesforce deployment tools.
Preferred: Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, CloudFormation, or other infrastructure-as-code technologies.
Preferred: Experience with event-driven architecture, Salesforce Platform Events, AWS EventBridge, SQS, SNS, or Kafka.
